items.title: 'What crime did we commit?': Indigenous leaders call for respect after Anzac booing
items.description: Indigenous elders face racist booing from crowd members at dawn services in Melbourne, Sydney and Perth, with one man arrested and charged over his alleged involvement and others issued with move-on orders.

items.title: AFL sacks appeals boss after homophobia statement labelled 'disgusting'
items.description: Will Houghton KC is sacked as the chair of the AFL appeals board after the body's widely criticised statement and decision in the case of St Kilda player Lance Collard.

items.title: Black Ferns outclass Wallaroos in Anzac Day Test
items.description: The Black Ferns produce a dominant performance to defeat the Wallaroos 40-5 in the first Anzac Day Test between the trans-Tasman rivals.

items.title: Live: Fremantle cruising towards big win as Carlton collapses in final quarter
items.description: Fremantle flexes its muscles to start the final quarter in Perth as an all-too familiar tale of fadeouts continues for Carlton after a gallant first three quarters. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Boos ring out, Storm fans head for exit as Souths thrash Melbourne
items.description: The South Sydney Rabbitohs have broken their hoodoo in Melbourne, smashing the Storm to achieve the club's first-ever win in the Victorian capital. Follow live.

items.title: From arrests to resignations, the Epstein fallout one year on from Virginia Giuffre's death
items.description: Virginia Giuffre didn't live to witness the full impact of the truths she brought forward, but the arrests, resignations and the unravelling of reputations came in the wake of her decision to speak.

items.title: Russian attack on Ukrainian apartment block kills seven, injures dozens
items.description: An apartment block in the south-eastern city of Dnipro was struck twice by Russian drones, officials say.

items.title: Third US aircraft enters waters near Iran carrying thousands more troops
items.description: USS George HW Bush has arrived in the Middle East, bringing thousands more American troops and advanced fighter jets to the region.

items.title: 'I saw a little nose poke around the corner': Puppy found after missing for months
items.description: A dachshund puppy is reunited with its owner after being lost for almost three months, in an adventure spanning multiple suburbs.

items.title: Sydney beaches closed after whale carcass attracts sharks
items.description: Several popular beaches in Sydney's Royal National Park are closed due to increased shark activity after a large whale carcass washes up on a rock platform.

items.title: Police say body found on Fleurieu Peninsula was murder victim
items.description: SA Police say initial investigations suggest a person whose body has been found in bushland south of Adelaide was murdered.

items.title: James Valentine knew good radio and I was his wide-eyed apprentice
items.description: As an aspiring broadcaster, I covertly watched everything James Valentine did on air. He taught me how in the absurd minutia of our lives, we reveal ourselves to each other.

items.title: Why Australia's weather map has ground to a halt
items.description: Darwin to Melbourne, and everywhere in between, the seven-day forecasts reveal a monotonous similarity.

items.title: One Nation's outcome in Farrer could be a watershed moment
items.description: The Coalition's preference deals in Farrer could help fracture the Liberal Party's moderate base and invigorate dissatisfied voters.

items.title: This easy 'hug in a bowl' chicken stew is perfect for midweek dinners
items.description: "It's a shortcut to that feeling that you get when you've slow cooked something all Sunday, but without that time or labour."

items.title: What happens to a relationship after a rural tree change
items.description: Director James Litchfield brings his experience growing up in rural Australia to his debut feature film, Alphabet Lane.

items.title: Quiz: Test yourself on The Shawshank Redemption, hair metal and Bugs Bunny
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right, and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: The details about an 'internationally acclaimed' artist that brought his identity undone
items.description: An Australian gallery has been selling sculptures as the work of an "internationally acclaimed" French artist. But the Paris backstory doesn’t stack up.

items.title: Dissecting the art of apologising, from MAFS men to Tucker Carlson
items.description: There's almost something weaponised about the contemporary apology, and perversely the social media culture that aims to teach self-awareness and accountability might just be responsible for it.

items.title: The chart that shows how much the NDIS price tag has blown out
items.description: An analysis of price forecasts in previous budgets reveals the NDIS was on track to cost more than four times what was initially expected.

items.title: Three men arrested after alleged arson attack in Melbourne CBD
items.description: Police were led on a foot-chase by alleged arsonists after a bar was set alight in ACDC lane early on Saturday morning.

items.title: Scrapped anti-whaling ship bought for $10 makes conservation comeback
items.description: The MV Steve Irwin anti-whaling vessel returns to marine conservation, restored to its former glory, after more than seven years out of action.

items.title: Couple rebuilds home after bushfire on condition it will never burn again
items.description: During the Black Summer bushfires, the Grahams watched their house burn from a peephole in a fire bunker. When they decided to rebuild, they created the most fire-resilient home possible. Here's how they did it.

items.title: Family keeps century-old farming trade alive
items.description: Brothers in northern NSW continue a tool trade that's more than 100 years old. They believe they are some of the last manufacturers of ear-marking pliers in Australia.

items.title: Industry 'alert but not alarmed' as native weevil develops a taste for cotton
items.description: Farmers and researchers notice a rise in bicoloured weevils feeding on cotton crops in the Northern Territory.
